title: Warning to the Wicked and the Self: Misuse of Human Faculties and Their 2 Main Purposes

questions.question: What did the bad group do when they came into the world and became old enough to choose?
questions.answer: They turned away from faith and did not respond in the right way.

questions.question: How did they treat Allah’s blessings?
questions.answer: They were unthankful.

questions.question: How did they treat other creatures?
questions.answer: They acted as if creatures had no worth and insulted them.

questions.question: Why was their wrong so serious?
questions.answer: Because they denied many signs that point to Allah and rejected His names.

questions.question: What did they deserve because of this big wrong?
questions.answer: Endless punishment.

questions.question: What were life and human abilities given for?
questions.answer: For important duties, not for doing wrong.

questions.question: Does the passage say our job in life is only to enjoy comfort and feed our bodies?
questions.answer: No. Life is for much more than that.

questions.question: Are our senses and body parts made only for low wants?
questions.answer: No. They have higher purposes.

questions.question: How many main purposes are named for the senses and abilities in us?
questions.answer: Two.

questions.question: What is the first main purpose?
questions.answer: To notice Allah’s blessings and thank and worship Him.

questions.question: What is the second main purpose?
questions.answer: To learn about Allah’s names through what we experience and then believe.

questions.question: What happens to a person who reaches these two purposes?
questions.answer: The person grows and becomes a real, complete human being.

questions.question: Which group is talked about in this passage?
questions.answer: The sinners and wicked people.

questions.question: When did they begin showing their wrong response?
questions.answer: When they entered life at the age when they could understand and choose.

questions.question: What did they do with the signs showing Allah’s oneness?
questions.answer: They refused to believe them.

questions.question: What did they do instead of being thankful for blessings?
questions.answer: They showed ingratitude.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the way they looked at creatures?
questions.answer: They treated them like they were worthless.

questions.question: Why did this become a huge crime?
questions.answer: Because they rejected the signs of Allah’s names.

questions.question: Did it take them a long time to earn blame for this?
questions.answer: No. They did this great wrong in a short time.

questions.question: What question is asked to wake up the careless self?
questions.answer: Whether life is only for a nice worldly life and body pleasure.

questions.question: What kinds of things inside us are mentioned as not being made just for low desires?
questions.answer: Our senses, feelings, body parts, and inner abilities.

questions.question: What is one reason these abilities were placed in us?
questions.answer: So we can know the many blessings of the True Giver.

questions.question: After knowing those blessings, what should a person do?
questions.answer: Thank Allah and worship Him.

questions.question: What is the other reason for these abilities?
questions.answer: So we can notice the signs of Allah’s holy names in the world, experience them, and believe.

questions.question: In the passage, what wrong answer did the wicked give to the signs of Allah’s unity?
questions.answer: They answered with unbelief.

questions.question: What wrong answer did they give to blessings?
questions.answer: They answered with thanklessness.

questions.question: What was insulting about the way they viewed creation?
questions.answer: They acted like creation had no value.

questions.question: What does the passage say they denied besides the signs of unity?
questions.answer: The displays of Allah’s names.

questions.question: Why are they said to deserve never-ending punishment?
questions.answer: Because they committed a very great wrong by rejecting all that.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the purpose of life’s “capital” and human powers?
questions.answer: They were given for special duties.

questions.question: What mistake does the speaker warn against about life’s purpose?
questions.answer: Thinking life is only for comfort, civilization, and satisfying the body.

questions.question: What mistake does the speaker warn against about our senses and limbs?
questions.answer: Thinking they are only for low desires in this short life.

questions.question: What strong phrase shows that this idea is very wrong?
questions.answer: A phrase meaning “Never!”

questions.question: What is the first big purpose for our being created this way?
questions.answer: To recognize Allah’s gifts and give thanks.

questions.question: What is the second big purpose?
questions.answer: To know Allah’s names through our experiences and come to faith.

questions.question: According to the end of the passage, how does a person become a true human?
questions.answer: By reaching those two main purposes.

questions.question: Who are the “other group” in this passage?
questions.answer: People who sin and act wickedly.

questions.question: What did they choose when they became responsible for their choices?
questions.answer: They chose unbelief.

questions.question: How did they act toward the many gifts given to them?
questions.answer: They did not show thanks.

questions.question: How did their attitude hurt the creatures around them?
questions.answer: They dishonored them by treating them as useless.

questions.question: What made their sin “boundless”?
questions.answer: They rejected the many signs and names that show Allah.

questions.question: What lesson is given about our life and abilities?
questions.answer: They were given for duties, not wasted living.

questions.question: Is a person’s mission just to enjoy modern life and bodily wants?
questions.answer: No. That is not the real mission.

questions.question: What parts of a person are listed as having a higher purpose?
questions.answer: Senses, abilities, organs, limbs, systems, and feelings.

questions.question: What is one purpose of these gifts inside us?
questions.answer: To help us notice Allah’s favors.

questions.question: What should come after noticing Allah’s favors?
questions.answer: Thankfulness and worship.

questions.question: How do our abilities help us know Allah in another way?
questions.answer: They help us experience signs of His names in the world.

questions.question: What comes from knowing those signs the right way?
questions.answer: Faith, growth, and becoming truly human.

questions.question: What happens when people answer Allah’s signs with unbelief?
questions.answer: They do a very serious wrong.

questions.question: What happens when people answer blessings with ingratitude?
questions.answer: They misuse what was given and fail in their duty.

questions.question: According to the passage, what was wrong with how the wicked treated creatures?
questions.answer: They looked down on them and insulted them.

questions.question: Why does the passage connect their actions to endless punishment?
questions.answer: Because they denied what should have led them to faith and thanks.

questions.question: What had been given to human beings that they used wrongly?
questions.answer: Life and human faculties.

questions.question: What false idea about life is challenged in the passage?
questions.answer: That life is only for pleasure and feeding the body.

questions.question: Why is that idea too small?
questions.answer: Because our abilities were made for higher goals.

questions.question: Name one group of things in us that the passage says has a higher purpose.
questions.answer: Our senses and feelings.

questions.question: What is the first of the two main aims named here?
questions.answer: To know the Giver’s many blessings.

questions.question: What should a person do after knowing those blessings?
questions.answer: Give thanks and worship Allah.

questions.question: What is the second main aim?
questions.answer: To know the displays of Allah’s names through our faculties.

questions.question: What is the result of living for these two aims?
questions.answer: A person matures and becomes a true human being.

questions.question: What kind of people are described at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: Wrongdoers who are sinful and wicked.

questions.question: What did they do to the proofs that point to one God?
questions.answer: They rejected them.

questions.question: What feeling did they fail to show for the gifts they received?
questions.answer: Gratitude.

questions.question: What does the passage say about their way of speaking about or treating creatures?
questions.answer: They treated them with disrespect, as if they were worthless.

questions.question: What else did they reject besides the proofs of Allah’s oneness?
questions.answer: The signs of Allah’s names.

questions.question: What was the outcome of that rejection?
questions.answer: They became deserving of endless punishment.

questions.question: What does the speaker ask the careless self not to think about life?
questions.answer: Not to think life is just for an easy, pleasure-filled worldly living.

questions.question: What does the passage say about our delicate senses and well-made body parts?
questions.answer: They are not only for low desires.

questions.question: How many great purposes are given for these human abilities?
questions.answer: Two great purposes.

questions.question: In simple words, what is the first purpose?
questions.answer: To recognize Allah’s blessings and thank Him.

questions.question: In simple words, what is the second purpose?
questions.answer: To notice Allah’s names through experience and believe in Him.

questions.question: If a person fulfills these two purposes, what does he or she become?
questions.answer: A true human being.
